::: {#exm-population-mean-uniform-limit}
#### Population means of finer and finer grids approach the expectation of a uniform variable

For a whole number $n \ge 1$, take the [finite](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mcs/functions.html#def-finite-set) population of $n$ evenly spaced values
$\frac{1}{n}, \frac{2}{n}, \ldots, \frac{n}{n}$ in the [interval](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mcs/sets.html#def-interval) $(0, 1]$.
By @prp-population-mean-expectation,
the [expectation](#def-expectation) of one value [chosen at random](probability-basics.qmd#def-random-choice) is the [population mean](#def-expectation):

$$
\ba
\avgin \frac{i}{n}
&= \frac{1}{n^2} \sumin i
&& \text{(take the constant } 1/n \text{ out of each term)}
\\&= \frac{1}{n^2} \cd \frac{n(n+1)}{2}
&& \text{(the sum of the first } n \text{ whole numbers)}
\\&= \frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{2n}
&& \text{(simplify)}
\ea
$$

As $n$ grows, the grid fills the interval,
and the population mean $\frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{2n}$ approaches $\frac{1}{2}$.
No finite population has every number in $[0, 1]$ as a unit,
but a [random variable](random-variables.qmd#def-random-variable) $X \sim \text{Uniform}(0, 1)$ ([uniform distribution](random-variables.qmd#def-uniform)) has [density](random-variables.qmd#def-pdf) $\p(X = x) = 1$ on $[0, 1]$,
and @def-expectation gives

$$
\ba
\E{X}
&= \int_0^1 x \cd 1 \,dx
&& \text{(definition of expectation, with density } 1 \text{)}
\\&= \frac{1}{2}
&& \text{(integrate)}
\ea
$$

the [limit](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/calculus-derivatives.html#def-limit) of the finite population means.
